questions.scenario: Winter is finally over, and Mummy tells you to pack away all the heavy blankets (razaais) and sweaters. What do you do?

options.text: Take the physical load, lift the heavy trunks and suitcases, and stuff them safely onto the top shelf (chhajja).
Calculate exactly how many mothballs (naphthalene) and vacuum bags are needed based on last year's winter packing.
Arrange the suitcases in a specific way to maximize the tiny storage space so it all fits perfectly.
Decide which old, torn sweaters should be donated or thrown away to optimize the total storage space in the house.

questions.scenario: You are desperately looking for a specific old notebook in your chaotic, messy study cupboard. How do you find it?

options.text: Empty the entire cupboard onto the bed, sit on the floor, and physically dig through every single pile.
Realize you have a pattern of losing math notebooks every term and decide to track your stationery better from now on.
Re-design the shelf layout so big textbooks go at the back and daily rough notebooks stay easily accessible in the front.
Make a strict rule that your sibling cannot touch your cupboard anymore so your stuff stops going missing.

questions.scenario: Mummy asks you to organize the kitchen pantry (masala boxes, dal jars, and snacks). What is your strategy?

options.text: Climb the stool, wipe down all the dusty jars, and actively shift the heavy 10kg rice and atta containers to the bottom.
Check the expiry dates on the Maggi packets and make a list of exactly how much sugar and dal is needed for the next grocery run.
Arrange the glass jars beautifully by color and size so the kitchen looks highly aesthetic and organized.
Convince Mummy to switch to an entirely new set of modular Tupperware containers to make daily cooking much faster.

questions.scenario: The school sports equipment room is a complete disaster, with balls and bats everywhere. How do you fix it?

options.text: Sort the deflated footballs from the good ones and physically stack the heavy cricket kits in the corner.
Look at the sports register to see how many badminton rackets go missing every month to predict the replacement cost.
Draw a mental map to figure out where to put new shelves so kids don't trip over the skipping ropes near the door.
Go to the Principal to request a budget for new sports gear and propose a strict 'sign-out' register system.

questions.scenario: It is Diwali Safai (cleaning) time! The whole house is upside down. What is your role?

options.text: Being the main 'worker' who pushes the heavy sofa and lifts the bed so the hidden corners can be swept.
Estimating how many cleaning cloths and Colin spray bottles you need so you don't run out midway through the day.
Suggesting a complete change in the furniture arrangement to make the living room feel much bigger and more spacious.
Assigning specific rooms to your siblings and managing the entire cleaning schedule so it finishes before lunch.

questions.scenario: Your class is organizing the food and game stalls for the massive school winter carnival. What are you handling?

options.text: Running back and forth carrying boxes of chart paper, glue, and heavy snack cartons from the gate to the stalls.
Calculating the exact number of samosas to order by analyzing last year's student attendance and sales data.
Planning the physical placement of the food stalls vs. the game stalls to avoid massive crowd jams and stampedes.
Managing the main cash box, paying the tent-wala bhaiya, and making sure nobody steals the extra supplies.

questions.scenario: Papa asks you to pack the car trunk (dickey) for a long family road trip to a hill station. How do you do it?

options.text: Shove the heavy suitcases in the back and use your physical strength to make sure the trunk closes perfectly.
Anticipate that you'll need the snack bag and jackets midway, so you logically keep them easily accessible at the top.
Treat it like a real-life game of Tetris, visualizing the perfect geometric fit for every single awkwardly shaped bag.
Instruct everyone beforehand to limit their luggage to one bag each so the car doesn't get overloaded and slow down.

questions.scenario: Your family is hosting a big dinner party and you need to bring extra chairs from the neighbors. What do you do?

options.text: Actually carry the stack of plastic chairs up the stairs and place them around the dining table.
Count the exact number of RSVP'd guests to ensure there isn't a shortage of plates, chairs, or spoons.
Figure out the best angle to place the chairs so people can easily walk to the buffet table without bumping elbows.
Coordinate with the caterer to ensure the food arrives exactly on time and manage the overall party budget.

questions.scenario: Moving day! Your family is shifting to a new flat. What catches your attention?

options.text: Directing the Packers & Movers, making sure the heavy fridge and washing machine don't scratch the walls.
Numbering all the 50 cardboard boxes and making a master Excel list to ensure absolutely nothing gets lost in transit.
Mentally picturing exactly where the TV unit and the L-shaped sofa will look best in the new living room layout.
Tipping the workers, handling the society entry pass, and making sure the entire shifting process stays within the budget.

questions.scenario: You are organizing your massive childhood collection of comic books or trading cards. What's your approach?

options.text: Sitting on the floor, dusting each book, and physically stacking them into tall, neat piles.
Realizing which rare cards will increase in value and tracking their current market demand online.
Buying transparent display cases and setting them up to look like a premium, mini-museum shelf in your room.
Deciding to sell the duplicates on OLX to make some pocket money and fund your next big purchase.

Floor_Supervisor.title: The Ground Commander (Floor & Inventory Supervisor)
Floor_Supervisor.primary_match_text: You love being active and getting things done with your own hands! You hate sitting behind a desk all day. You are practical, energetic, and love the satisfaction of physically organizing a chaotic space.
Floor_Supervisor.day_in_the_life: Running around massive warehouses the size of football fields, managing incoming delivery trucks, directing forklifts, and making sure thousands of packages are stored safely.
Floor_Supervisor.alternative_match_text: Your high energy and practical skills would also make you a fantastic Event Operations Manager, Retail Store Manager, or Site Supervisor.
Floor_Supervisor.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Any Stream (Commerce preferred). Degree: BBA in Logistics, Supply Chain Management, or B.Com. Next Steps: Take on ground-level operations internships at massive e-commerce hubs like Amazon or Flipkart.

Inventory_Forecaster.title: The Prediction Genius (Demand & Inventory Forecaster)
Inventory_Forecaster.primary_match_text: You are a master of logic and planning! You love analyzing data, finding patterns, and predicting the future. You don't just organize things; you calculate exactly how much of everything will be needed.
Inventory_Forecaster.day_in_the_life: Looking at massive data dashboards, predicting how many iPhones or winter jackets an entire city will buy next month, and making sure the warehouse never runs out of stock.
Inventory_Forecaster.alternative_match_text: Your highly analytical brain makes you a perfect fit for Data Analytics, Financial Planning, or Market Research.
Inventory_Forecaster.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Commerce with Math or PCM. Degree: B.Sc in Statistics, B.Tech, or BBA in Data Analytics. Next Steps: Learn advanced Excel, Python, and pursue an MBA in Supply Chain & Operations.

Layout_Designer.title: The Space Architect (Warehouse Layout Designer)
Layout_Designer.primary_match_text: You have an amazing spatial awareness and a highly creative brain. You treat real-world spaces like a puzzle. You love figuring out the most efficient, beautiful, and smartest way to arrange things.
Layout_Designer.day_in_the_life: Designing 3D floor plans on software, figuring out the fastest routes for warehouse robots to move, and ensuring massive storage racks are placed perfectly for maximum efficiency.
Layout_Designer.alternative_match_text: If not logistics, your spatial creativity would make you a brilliant Industrial Designer, Architect, or Civil Engineer.
Layout_Designer.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Science (PCM is highly recommended). Degree: B.Tech/B.E. in Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or Civil Engineering. Next Steps: Master AutoCAD and 3D modeling software.

Warehouse_Manager.title: The Operations Boss (Facility / Warehouse Manager)
Warehouse_Manager.primary_match_text: You are a natural leader and a big-picture thinker. You understand the value of organization, but you prefer managing the people, the budget, and the overall strategy. You like being in charge.
Warehouse_Manager.day_in_the_life: Managing a million-dollar facility, ensuring 500+ staff members are working safely, negotiating with transport vendors, and making sure the entire warehouse runs profitably.
Warehouse_Manager.alternative_match_text: Your leadership and management skills would make you an excellent Project Manager, Corporate Operations Head, or Entrepreneur.
Warehouse_Manager.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Commerce or PCM. Degree: BBA, B.Com, or B.Tech. Next Steps: Gain a few years of core corporate experience, then crack CAT/GMAT to pursue an MBA in Operations Management.
